answer: In a weather-data exchange, each agent bonds a registered station with a prism for light readings and a crystal clock. When a surprise gale arrives, the station signs raw measurements; independent nearby stations compare timing and conditions. Rewards are capped at one per verified site, so ten aliases controlling one sensor earn one share. An attacker seeking ten shares must buy and place ten sensors and lock ten bonds. Rental hardware and colluding stations could still spoof independence, so random site audits remain necessary.
